cards.name: Adobe PDF Presets
cards.summary: Opens the Adobe PDF Presets dialog, where the named PDF export settings (.joboptions files shared by the Creative Cloud apps, e.g. [High Quality Print], [Press Quality], [PDF/X-4:2008], [Smallest File Size]) are created, edited, deleted, imported and exported. It manages presets only; it does not save a PDF. Enabled with no document open.
cards.how: Pick a preset to read its description, then New or Edit to set compatibility, PDF/X standard, image compression, marks and bleeds, output colour conversion and security; Load / Save As move .joboptions files between machines or from a print shop. Built-in presets (in square brackets) cannot be edited, only used as the starting point of a New one.
use_for: setting up a print shop's PDF/X preset once so posters, flyers and packaging comps export to the same spec
making a small-file preset for emailing client proofs
loading the .joboptions a printer sent so Photoshop, Illustrator and InDesign all export alike
avoid: actually exporting the file: use File > Save As (Photoshop PDF) and pick the preset there
editing a built-in preset expecting it to change: start a New preset from it instead
cards.script_api: No script route harvested for managing presets (no menuItemType or event label matches; menu command id 1215 is not runnable through runMenuItem). To export WITH a preset instead: PDFSaveOptions.presetFile (a writable member in the PS API harvest, not run) takes the preset name, then app.activeDocument.saveAs(file, opts).

review.changes: script_api presented PDFSaveOptions.presetFile + saveAs as this command without its dialog, but it exports with a preset rather than managing presets; reworded, and presetFile cited from the PS API harvest. Preset names checked against the shared .joboptions in harvest/ai/ai_preset.json

cards.name: Assign Profile
cards.summary: Tags the active document with a different ICC profile (or none) without changing its pixel numbers, so the same values are interpreted, displayed and printed as a different colour space; the image visibly shifts colour. Needs an open document.
cards.how: Three choices: Don't Color Manage This Document, Working RGB/CMYK (the space from Color Settings), or Profile (pick any installed profile from the list). Preview shows the shift live. The profile is embedded on save when Embed Color Profile is on.
use_for: tagging an untagged camera or client file with the space it was actually made in (e.g. sRGB or Adobe RGB) so it previews correctly
fixing a file that was opened with the wrong profile assumption
checking how the same CMYK numbers would look under a different press profile
avoid: converting an image to a new output space (web sRGB, press CMYK) while keeping its look: use Edit/Convert to Profile
changing the colour mode only: use Image > Mode
cards.script_api: executeAction(stringIDToTypeID('assignProfile'), desc, DialogModes.NO) with desc: null = reference to the document (Dcmn), profile (string) = 'Adobe RGB (1998)'; verified live (profile sRGB IEC61966-2.1 -> Adobe RGB (1998)). DOM alternative: app.activeDocument.colorProfileName = 'Adobe RGB (1998)' (a writable member in the PS API harvest, not run).

review.changes: script_api: colorProfileName is a writable Document member in the PS API harvest, so the DOM route now cites it (still not run)

cards.name: Auto-Align Layers
cards.summary: Analyses the content of two or more selected layers and moves, scales, rotates or warps them so matching features line up, for example the overlapping frames of a panorama or a bracketed or handheld burst. Needs two or more layers selected.
cards.how: Projection: Auto, Perspective, Collage, Cylindrical, Spherical or Reposition (Reposition only shifts; Collage allows rotate and scale only). Lens Correction: Vignette Removal and Geometric Distortion for wide-angle sources. Follow with Auto-Blend Layers to hide the seams.
use_for: lining up overlapping photos before stitching a panorama for a wide hero banner
aligning a handheld bracketed or focus-stack series before blending
aligning several group-photo frames so the best faces can be masked in
avoid: aligning layer edges or centres for layout: use the Move tool's align buttons or Layer > Align
layers with little overlapping detail (flat colour, text): the match fails or warps badly
cards.script_api: executeAction(stringIDToTypeID('align'), desc, DialogModes.ALL) with desc: null = reference to layers (Lyr), using (Usng) = enum alignDistributeSelector 'ADSContent'; run live on a multi-layer scratch document (history state 'Align content'). DialogModes.ALL shows the dialog; DialogModes.NO with the same descriptor should run without it (unverified).

review.changes: none

cards.name: Auto-Blend Layers
cards.summary: Blends two or more selected, already aligned layers into one seamless result by giving each layer a layer mask that hides its seams or its out-of-focus areas: Panorama mode stitches overlapping frames, Stack Images mode keeps the sharpest parts of each layer for a focus stack. Needs two or more layers selected.
cards.how: Blend Method: Panorama or Stack Images. Seamless Tones and Colors evens out exposure and colour across the seams; Content Aware Fill Transparent Areas fills the empty corners a panorama leaves. Run Auto-Align Layers first.
use_for: finishing a stitched panorama for a wide web banner or print backdrop
focus-stacking product macro shots so the whole product is sharp
merging aligned frames of the same scene into one clean plate
avoid: layers that are not aligned yet: run Edit/Auto-Align Layers first
blending unrelated images for a creative composite: paint layer masks by hand instead
cards.script_api: executeAction(stringIDToTypeID('mergeAlignedLayers'), new ActionDescriptor(), DialogModes.NO); verified live on a multi-layer scratch document (a layer mask appeared on the layer; history 'Auto-Blend Layers').

review.changes: none

cards.name: Check Spelling
cards.summary: Opens the Check Spelling dialog and steps through the words in the document's text layers that are not in the dictionary of each text's language, offering suggestions. Pixel text (rasterised type) is not checked. Needs an open document.
cards.how: For each flagged word: Ignore, Ignore All, Change (to the selected suggestion or a typed word), Change All, or Add to the user dictionary. Check All Layers checks every text layer instead of only the selected one. The dictionary follows the Language set in the Character panel.
use_for: proofing headline and body copy on a poster or social post before export
catching typos in a menu, flyer or banner set built in Photoshop
avoid: text that has been rasterised or is in a placed image: retype it as live type first
replacing one word everywhere: use Edit/Find and Replace Text
cards.script_api: executeAction(stringIDToTypeID('spellCheck'), undefined, DialogModes.ALL) opens the Check Spelling dialog (verified live); there is no known no-dialog route.

review.changes: none

cards.name: Clear
cards.summary: Deletes the pixels inside the active selection on the active layer without putting them on the clipboard, leaving a transparent hole; on the Background layer the area is filled with the background colour instead. Needs an active selection.
use_for: knocking a shape out of a texture layer
removing a background area after a Select Subject or Magic Wand selection
clearing a block of a layer to make room for a headline
avoid: cutting pixels you want to paste elsewhere: use Edit/Cut
edits you may want to undo later: hide the area with a layer mask instead (non-destructive)
cards.script_api: app.activeDocument.selection.clear() (verified live: history 'Clear' after a lasso selection).

review.changes: none

cards.name: Color Settings
cards.summary: Opens the Color Settings dialog that sets Photoshop's application-wide colour management: the working RGB, CMYK, Gray and Spot spaces, what happens when a file's embedded profile does not match, and how colours are converted. Enabled with no document open.
cards.how: Settings presets (regional General Purpose, Prepress and Web sets) set everything at once. Working Spaces pick the default profiles; Color Management Policies choose Preserve Embedded Profiles, Convert to Working, or Off, with Ask When Opening / Pasting for mismatches and missing profiles. Conversion Options set the engine, rendering intent, black point compensation and dither. Save / Load share a .csf file.
use_for: setting the studio's CMYK working space to the printer's press profile before building print artwork
making Photoshop ask before converting client files that carry a different profile
matching colour settings across the Creative Cloud apps for a print job
avoid: changing one document's profile: use Edit/Assign Profile or Edit/Convert to Profile
screen soft-proofing: use View > Proof Setup
cards.script_api: app.runMenuItem(stringIDToTypeID('colorSettings')) opens the dialog (verified live). Without the dialog: app.colorSettings = '<settings name>' (a writable Application member in the PS API harvest, not run).

cards.name: Content-Aware Fill
cards.summary: Opens the Content-Aware Fill workspace, which fills the selected area with texture synthesised from a sampling area of the surrounding image, so an unwanted object or blemish disappears into its background. Needs an active selection around the object.
cards.how: Paint or adjust the sampling area (green overlay; Auto, Rectangular or Custom). Fill Settings: Color Adaptation, Rotation Adaptation, Scale and Mirror help with gradients, curves and symmetric scenes. Output To: Current Layer, New Layer or Duplicate Layer. The preview updates live; OK applies.
use_for: removing a sign, wire or passer-by from a background photo before placing a headline
extending a sky or wall to clean up a product shot
cleaning dust, logos or watermarks off a stock plate you have rights to edit
avoid: large or structured areas (faces, text, repeated architecture): the synthesis repeats patterns; use Edit/Generative Fill or clone by hand
selections tight to the object: expand the selection a few pixels first or edges ghost
cards.script_api: executeAction(stringIDToTypeID('cafWorkspace'), new ActionDescriptor(), DialogModes.NO); verified live: with no settings it applied the fill with the workspace defaults and the result landed on a new layer.

review.changes: none

cards.name: Content-Aware Scale
cards.summary: Puts the active layer (or the selected area) into a scaling mode that resizes the image while protecting its important content: flat or low-detail regions such as sky, water or plain wall are stretched or squeezed first, so people and objects keep their proportions. Needs an open document; it is unavailable for text layers, smart objects, groups and multiple selected layers.
cards.how: Drag the transform handles or type W/H in the options bar. Amount (a percentage) blends between content-aware and normal scaling; Protect picks an alpha channel whose white areas must not distort; the person icon protects skin tones. Commit with the options-bar tick.
use_for: turning a landscape photo into a wider banner or narrower story format without cropping the subject
making room beside a subject for headline copy
adapting one key visual to several aspect ratios
avoid: big changes in proportion with busy backgrounds: distortion and warping appear; add canvas with the Crop Tool instead (its Generative Expand fills the new area)
text, smart objects and groups: rasterise or work on a flattened copy first
cards.script_api: app.runMenuItem(stringIDToTypeID('contentAware')) is the label-matched candidate (not run: it enters an interactive transform mode that waits for the user to commit).

review.changes: how: removed the unharvested 0-100% Amount range and the Enter key; avoid: Generative Expand named as the Crop Tool option it is (no such menu command in the harvest)

cards.name: Convert to Profile
cards.summary: Converts the active document's pixel values from its current profile into another ICC profile so the image looks as close as possible to before in the new space (for example Adobe RGB to sRGB for web, or RGB to a press CMYK profile, which also changes the mode). Needs an open document.
cards.how: Pick the Destination Space profile. Conversion Options: Engine (Adobe ACE), Intent (Perceptual, Relative Colorimetric, Saturation, Absolute Colorimetric), Use Black Point Compensation, Use Dither. Flatten Image to Preserve Appearance merges layers so blend modes look the same after conversion. Advanced shows multichannel profiles.
use_for: converting a finished social graphic to sRGB before export so colours do not shift online
converting a poster to the printer's CMYK profile for press
standardising a set of mixed-profile stock photos to one working space
avoid: fixing a file that merely previews wrongly: use Edit/Assign Profile (tags without converting)
converting back and forth repeatedly: each conversion loses colour data, keep an RGB master
cards.script_api: executeAction(stringIDToTypeID('convertToProfile'), desc, DialogModes.NO) with desc: null = reference to the document (Dcmn), T (charID 'T   ') = 'Adobe RGB (1998)'; verified live. Note: with only that key the harvest saw the layered scratch document flattened to a single Background layer, so set the flatten option off (key unverified) or run it on a copy. DOM alternative: app.activeDocument.convertProfile('sRGB IEC61966-2.1', Intent.RELATIVECOLORIMETRIC, true, true) (destinationProfile, intent, blackPointCompensation, dither in the PS API harvest; not run).

cards.name: Copy

duplicating a texture patch to paste over a blemish
moving artwork from Photoshop into Illustrator or another app via the clipboard
avoid: copying what you see across all visible layers: use Edit/Copy Merged
duplicating a whole layer inside the same document: Layer/Duplicate Layer keeps its layer styles, mask and smart object; Layer/New/Layer Via Copy puts the selected pixels on a new layer in place

cards.name: Copy Merged
cards.summary: Copies the selected area as it looks with all visible layers combined (a flattened snapshot of the selection) to the clipboard, without merging or changing any layer. Needs an active selection.
use_for: grabbing a finished composite area to paste as one layer for a final sharpen or grade
pasting a flattened crop of a layered layout into another document or app
making a quick flattened sample for a thumbnail
avoid: copying only the active layer's pixels: use Edit/Copy
a flattened layer of the whole document inside the same file: Select All, Copy Merged, then Edit/Paste Special/Paste in Place keeps it aligned

cards.name: Cut
cards.summary: Removes the pixels inside the active selection from the active layer and puts them on the clipboard, leaving a transparent hole (filled with the background colour on the Background layer). Needs an active selection.
use_for: moving part of an image to its own document or layer via paste
lifting an object out of a photo to reposition it
moving a block of pixels between documents

separating an area onto its own layer in place: Layer/New/Layer Via Cut keeps its position

cards.name: Define Brush Preset
cards.summary: Turns the selected area (or the whole image when nothing is selected) into a new brush tip and adds it to the Brushes panel; the tip is greyscale, so dark pixels paint opaque and light pixels paint faint. Asks for a name in the Brush Name dialog. Needs an open document.
cards.how: Make the source art black on white (or on transparency), select it, run the command and type the name in the Brush Name dialog. Afterwards set spacing, scattering and dynamics in Brush Settings and save the variant.
use_for: making a brush from a logo mark or ink splatter for stamping textures
creating grunge, dust or paper-grain brushes for poster backgrounds
turning a hand-drawn stroke into a reusable custom brush
avoid: keeping the art's colours: brush tips are greyscale; use a pattern or a placed image instead
tiled repeating fills: use Edit/Define Pattern

cards.name: Fade
cards.summary: Right after a filter, adjustment, fill or paint stroke, reduces the strength of that last operation and/or changes the blend mode it was applied with, as if it had been applied on a layer above at lower opacity. use_for: toning down a sharpening or blur pass on a portrait
applying a filter in Luminosity or Overlay mode for a subtle texture
softening a heavy adjustment on a photo backdrop
avoid: anything you may change later: apply the filter as a smart filter or the adjustment as an adjustment layer and lower its opacity instead

cards.name: OpenColorIO Settings
cards.summary: Opens the settings for Photoshop's OpenColorIO (OCIO) colour management, the configuration-based alternative to ICC profiles used in film and VFX pipelines (e.g. ACES): which OCIO configuration file is used and its default colour spaces. Enabled with no document open. The dialog's exact options were not harvested. In this build it is the only visible OpenColorIO command: File/New OpenColorIO, File/Open as OpenColorIO, Edit/Convert to OpenColorIO and Window/OpenColorIO are all hidden.
cards.how: Not harvested. Expect to choose an OCIO config (built-in or a .ocio file) and the working and display colour spaces that documents managed by OCIO use.
use_for: matching Photoshop to a studio's ACES/OCIO pipeline for matte paintings and VFX plates
keeping colour consistent with compositing apps that read the same OCIO config
avoid: print and web design colour setup: use Edit/Color Settings (ICC)
expecting to start an OCIO-managed document afterwards: the commands that create or convert one are hidden in the harvested build
cards.script_api: No script route harvested (no menuItemType or event label matches; menu command id 2345 is not runnable through runMenuItem).

review.changes: summary / avoid: the ps_menu harvest shows every other OCIO command hidden in this build, so a configured setting has no visible document command to use it; said so

cards.name: Paste
cards.summary: Pastes the clipboard into the active document as a new layer; pixels land centred (in the harvest, a 160 px tile copied at 40,40 landed centred on the 400x300 canvas), not at the copied position. Vector art from Illustrator brings up a Paste dialog (Smart Object, Pixels, Path or Shape Layer). Needs clipboard content.
use_for: bringing a copied cut-out or texture into a layout
pasting Illustrator logo art as a vector smart object
pasting copied text into a text layer while editing type
avoid: keeping the original position: use Paste Special/Paste in Place
pasting into a selection-shaped mask: use Paste Special/Paste Into
cards.script_api: executeAction(stringIDToTypeID('paste'), new ActionDescriptor(), DialogModes.NO) (verified live: new layer 'Layer 1' centred). DOM alternative: app.activeDocument.paste() (in the PS API harvest, not run).

review.changes: equivalents.CDR: CorelDRAW's Edit/Paste keeps the copied coordinates (that is Paste in Place); Edit/Paste in View is the centre-in-view counterpart; script_api: DOM call marked harvested but not run

cards.name: Paste in Place
cards.summary: Pastes the clipboard as a new layer at exactly the position it was copied from (in the harvest, copied at 40,40 and pasted at 40,40), instead of centring it. Needs clipboard content.
use_for: moving a retouch patch between two same-size versions of a layout without shifting it
copying elements between documents that share a grid or template
re-pasting a cut area back where it came from on a new layer
avoid: documents of different sizes when position does not matter: plain Edit/Paste is fine
pasting inside a selection mask: use Paste Special/Paste Into
cards.script_api: executeAction(stringIDToTypeID('paste'), desc, DialogModes.NO) with desc: inPlace (boolean) = true; verified live (pasted bounds equal the copied bounds).

review.changes: none

cards.name: Paste Into
cards.summary: Pastes the clipboard into a new layer whose layer mask is made from the active selection, so the pasted image shows only inside the selected shape; the mask is unlinked, so the image can be moved inside the frame. Needs clipboard content and an active selection.
use_for: dropping a photo into a window, screen or frame shape of a mock-up
filling headline letters (selected from type) with an image
placing a sky into the selected sky area of a photo
avoid: shapes you will edit or reuse: a clipping mask over a shape or type layer stays editable
showing the image outside the selection: use Paste Special/Paste Outside
cards.script_api: executeAction(stringIDToTypeID('pasteInto'), new ActionDescriptor(), DialogModes.NO) (verified live: new layer with an unlinked user mask, selection consumed). DOM alternative: app.activeDocument.paste(true) (intoSelection = true in the PS API harvest; not run).

review.changes: equivalents: added CDR Object/PowerClip/Place Inside Frame (places content inside a frame shape, the same job); script_api: paste(intoSelection) cited from the PS API harvest

cards.name: Paste Outside
cards.summary: Pastes the clipboard into a new layer whose layer mask is the inverse of the active selection, so the pasted image shows everywhere except inside the selected area; the mask is unlinked so the image can be repositioned. Needs clipboard content and an active selection.
use_for: replacing everything around a selected subject with a new background
framing a selected area with a pasted texture border
putting a pattern around a protected product area
avoid: showing the image only inside the selection: use Paste Special/Paste Into
complex cut-outs: build the mask with Select and Mask first, then paste
